title: Favorite trombonists: Baptiste and Frankie Dusen
summary: Morris names the trombonists he admired as a boy, Baptiste and valve player Frankie Dusen of the Eagle band, and how Dusen learned to read.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Who were some of the trombonists you liked when you were a boy and young? Who were the best? Who were the best?
Baptiste De Niel That's the one that I always did like I just used to like to see him pull that one, you know
Did he play valve or trombone?
No, it was slide Slide Yes, but I'll tell you who used to play a good vowel trombone, Frankie Dewson Yeah, Frankie Dewson used to play a good vowel trombone
Now how did he compare with Baptiste De Niel?

Who, Frankie Dewson? Oh, he couldn't compare with him, but he just had the break, you know, for the outside people And for Jerry's stuff, he had it But Baptiste De Niel, them were real people, you know, they just hit it right now And John Robich, sure, he used to teach them fellas See, you had to rehearse there for the letters twice a day, I think But I know you could go every day around 2 o'clock and you'd yum rehearse and in the back there
Did Frankie Dewson read music much?
Well, he could read it by getting with the good fellas, you know, which you didn't know they'd show it to you That's the way you get the music part
Who did Dewson play with when you heard him, do you remember his band?
The Eagle band Yes, that was his band, the Eagle band That was Frankie Dewson band
Who was in the Eagle with him, you know any of those guys?
Oh, I just remember who all was in the Eagle now They all dead now
